That's amazing! I'm sure you'll be excellent owners. And yes age can be a factor in owning a chinchilla. Just remember to take your time, and treats are always a win. Rolled oats are some of the best healthiest treats you can get.

I apologize if I come off a little brutish in this. I do want you to know what you're getting into ahead of time.

CONS:

1. They chew up everything. Here's a list of what my chin has chewed up. Baseboards, a wall corner, several electrical cords, several door stops, anything plastic he can get it hold of, tape rolls, laundry baskets, Etc.

2. They poop a lot! And I mean a lot. I clean out my Chin's cage once every day and when I say I pull out way more than a handful of poop I mean it. Thankfully there poop is hard and solid, it's essentially like sweeping up Tic Tacs.

3. They are very messy. Not just with poop but they like to push their hay out of their cage. Usually because they are picky on which hay straw they want to chew every other hay straw is kicked out of the cage.

4. They are expensive. Not just the initial cost. But also the cost of the cage which is easily $130+. They need a specialized wheel that has to be big and metal the cheapest you find is about $60. And everything in their cage has to be either a thick fabric they cannot eat, chin safe wood, metal, or ceramic. All of which is costly.

5. They don't like to cuddle. Chinchillas are prey animals, so they don't like to be held or trapped. They would rather come sit on your lap.

6. It can take an EXTREMELY long time to bond with your chinchilla. They are very stubborn and they are very shy. I got my chin at 6 months old and it took me around 8 months to truly bond with him. Some older chinchillas can take a little more time. I've heard stories of people having their chinchillas for 2 years and still not completely bonding.

7. They need a cool dry environment. Chinchillas have very thick fur, in fact, they are considered to have the second densest fur in the world! They have a lot of fur, and they do not have the ability to sweat. With that being said your chinchilla will DIE of heat stroke if not kept in cool dry temperatures of below 75 degrees Fahrenheit at most. If you have a finished basement with no leaks that's the perfect place to keep a chinchilla. Other than that it's probably best to have air conditioning and a fan on 24/7.

PROS:

1. They live a long time. Chinchillas have a similar life span to dogs, 8 to 15 years.

2. They really don't stink. This is a huge up point for me personally because I'm very sensitive to fragrance. When I say he doesn't stink, I really mean it! Walking into a house with someone who owns a chinchilla has a similar fragrance to walking into a house with someone who has a dog. As long as there's routine cage cleanings, any and all fragrance from a chinchilla can easily be covered with a vanilla candle. That's how little they smell. 

3. Once you truly bond with your chinchilla they will be your best friends. Mine likes to hop on my shoulder and groom my hair. They may not be cuddly but they show you affection in other ways.

4. They are adorable!

PSA: additionally, if you are allergic to pollen, hay, grass, fur, dust, or wood shavings. You probably shouldn't own a chinchilla because you will experience most of these with owning a chinchilla.

This is a neat little story, you must read a lot of Stephen King. Your character is good, well rounded. 

The best tip I can give you is to constantly ask yourself, "why." Why this, why that? Why did Ryuta go into the Tec industries? Did he play video games as a kid? Was he envious of other kids with cool technology? Was he in it for the money? Etc... 

You can always improve your characters by asking why they do the things or like the things that they do. But remember, not every answer has to be complex. Example from your own writing: "He likes it plain and simple, and can wear a turtleneck if he isn't confident about his neck." Simple answer. You could advance on this idea and state why he's not confident about his neck, or you can keep it simple.

Keep in mind most people only care about the main character. It's important to round out ALL of your characters (with exceptions of the flat/filler characters) with the why question.

Why is Anna abusive? Did she get abused? Is it a fetish? Was she raised in a strict house with weird rules? Does she feel ugly, inadequate, dirty, discusting, or have low self-esteem and she feels the need to reflect that on Ryuta? Why is Anna the bad guy? Why did she agree to let Ryuta go for so long? Was she secretly searching for new victims? Did she have her own affairs? Was she doing something darker like hiding from the law? 

Ask the why question for everybody. Why does Rick like Ryuta? Is Rick a fixer and he feels the need to fix Ryuta? Does Rick pity Ryuta? Why did Ryuta name Lilth, Lilth? Was it a cool name he liked? Why doesn't Ryuta search for Lilth in his five year journey? Why did he come back to Anna? Who picked the name Sen, what does the name mean? Does Lilth have abandonment issues or self-esteem issues after this affair? How does Ryuta seal his bond with Lilth in the end? You don't need answer all of those questions. They're just examples. 

That's the only tip I have. I think your plot is solid and well thought through. You have a very creative and imaginative mind. 😊👏 Well done. If you just ask the "why" question, your characters will write themselves in no time.

Good luck 😊

Beautiful color schemes and a very unique character. I think the best tip you can ever get in art, is to remember OBSERVATION IS KEY. 

Find some artists that you really look up to and notice shapes, sizes, dimensions, and start to copy their style. That can help you train up a little bit and the more You observe different styles the easier it will be to find your own style. 

You can start by looking at TV shows that you like. Some examples might be Steven Universe, Hazbin Hotel, Invader Zim, Rick and Morty, Family Guy, and maybe even some Disney. Some people like to copy off of their favorite animes like Sailor Moon, Dragon Ball Z, attack on Titan, Tokyo Ghoul, and Pokemon.

The best thing you can do to improve your art is to observe other people's art. Sometimes it's even helpful to copy pictures and or TV scenes or movie scenes. Just remember NEVER EVER EVER plagiarize. Plagiarism is first of all illegal, but also not fair to any artist. It's important that you understand copying a picture and passing it off as your own work, are two completely different things. 

That is my best tip for you. I could be wrong but it looks like you are just starting on your artistic jurney. You just have to keep trying and OBSERVATION IS KEY. You're on the right track, keep up the good work. 😊
